name: Naive Voxel Geometry

# Naive Voxel Geometry


## Overview
Naive Voxel Geometry is a family of [object-order volume rendering](#10725-object-order-volume-rendering.md) techniques that represent scalar field data as explicit geometric primitives (typically cubes or quads) submitted to the graphics pipeline for rasterization [G]. It differs from [image-order ray-casting](#3161-image-order-ray-casting.md) by projecting geometry into screen space rather than sampling rays through the volume [G], and from optimized variants like [Sparse Voxel Rasterization](3032-sparse-voxel-rasterization.md) by generating primitives for all voxels without Level of Detail (LOD) reduction or greedy meshing, resulting in massive vertex counts for large scenes [G].

## Shared principles
This family shares the fundamental mechanism of converting scalar field data into geometric primitives that are submitted to the graphics pipeline, as detailed in the parent article [Voxels rasterized as geometry](27-voxels-rasterized-as-geometry.md) [G].

## Subtopics

### [Naive Voxel Rendering](1103-naive-voxel-rendering.md)
An object-order technique that renders every visible voxel as an individual geometric primitive (typically a cube or cuboid) without merging adjacent faces into larger meshes or using Level of Detail (LOD) reduction. It solves the problem of visualizing volumetric data by directly rasterizing the underlying voxel grid geometry. Unlike [Base Renderer Geometry](3902-base-renderer-geometry.md) which may optimize mesh generation, this method explicitly avoids greedy meshing or [face culling](#8735-face-culling.md) between adjacent voxels, drawing every face of every active voxel individually.

### [Base Renderer Geometry](3902-base-renderer-geometry.md)
A method for rendering voxel data by converting occupied voxel cells into explicit geometric primitives (cubes, squares, or lines) and submitting them to the graphics pipeline for rasterization. It solves the problem of visualizing scalar field data by treating voxels as discrete mesh objects rather than ray-marching a volume. It differs from [Naive Voxel Rendering](1103-naive-voxel-rendering.md) by explicitly generating vertex/index buffers for geometry submission, and from [Cube Geometry for Volume Rendering](10885-cube-geometry-for-volume-rendering.md) by supporting multiple primitive topologies (faces, lines, full cubes) and dynamic batching strategies.

### [Cube Geometry for Volume Rendering](10885-cube-geometry-for-volume-rendering.md)
Represents a single occupied voxel as a simple [axis-aligned cube](#10885-cube-geometry-for-volume-rendering.md) primitive submitted to the graphics pipeline. It solves the problem of mapping discrete scalar field data to geometric primitives for rasterization. It differs from [Naive Voxel Rendering](1103-naive-voxel-rendering.md) by explicitly generating vertex and index buffers for a 3D box rather than using point sprites or billboarded quads, and from [Base Renderer Geometry](3902-base-renderer-geometry.md) by using a fixed, non-adaptive cube topology for every voxel.

### [Chunk-based Voxel Rendering Pipeline](14105-chunk-based-voxel-rendering-pipeline.md)
A high-throughput [object-order rendering](#22-object-order-rendering.md) method that aggregates voxel faces into geometric chunks, transforms them to [world space](#2511-voxel-coordinate-systems-and-conversion.md), and rasterizes them using a [Painter's Algorithm](#12692-back-to-front-rendering.md). It differs from naive voxel geometry by batching visible faces into chunks and applying distance-based sorting and horizon [clipping](#1444-clipping.md) to manage depth ordering and visual effects, rather than rendering individual voxels independently.
